title: The element sets of RouteRequest and Approval and the committee elements of the route answer are not published
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T-A.1, T-A.2); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.9.3.2, A2.9.4.1); Recovery Workbench Epics 3 to 8 Specification v3 (FEAT-VAL-09); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-009 Endpoints); 22 Microservice Realignment/Recovery Workbench Microservice Story Template and Rules v1.md (R9)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s4 Flow steps 2 and 3; s12.1 REST operations provided; s12.7 Tables owned; s12.8 Contract fakes; s13; s16 C2 and C7. APP s3; s7 Acceptance criteria; s11 Data; s12.1
description: TSD S1 T-A.2 names the operation only by its two types, RouteRequest in and Approval out, with the error set and the idempotency header, and publishes no field table for either. The FSD field catalog of A2.9.3.2 is the appraisal catalog of v_ace_valuation and valuation_ext and carries no route-answer element, and the legacy Endpoints table gives the path and the right with no element list. Three slices of this service therefore share one path with no published element set: the appraisal branch, the inside-limit approval and this committee branch. The baseline declares the committee elements the requirement and the routing rows name - the escalation and its item reference, the limit applied with its level and matrix version, the delegation version, the final call, the coded reason, the elapsed clock and the committee reference - as an additive extension of the element set the sibling baselines start, and marks the rest open.
evidence: TSD S1 T-A.2 is a seven-row item table naming Purpose, Request RouteRequest, Response Approval, Errors 401 to 503, Authorization, Idempotency and no field list; FSD S1 A2.9.3.2 lists v_ace_valuation.valuation_key to valuation_ext.valuer_partner_id and no route element; the legacy Endpoints table of RWB-E4-009 has one row, POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/route, Treatment and offer U; FSD S1 A2.9.4.1 has one main-flow account row.
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P3 rwb-case and P7 rwb-decision owners
proposed: The three slices agree one element set at the RWB-S1-E4009-CON tag, the owners of rwb-case and rwb-decision confirm the committee elements, and a published schema replaces the declared compacts in a minor version with no behaviour change.

title: The delegation-of-authority limit, its boundaries and the row that answers them are not published, and its owner is read two ways in this run
source: Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.9.3.1, A2.9.3.3); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.1, T6.1); Recovery Workbench Architecture v5 (slide 3, DoA Matrix v2); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-009 Data); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1 RWB-S1 E4008 (inside-limit slice of the same operation); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Service Story Files v1 RWB-S2 E3003 (below-floor approval of rwb-treatment)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s8 BR4; s11 Data; s12.2 REST operations consumed; s12.8 Contract fakes; s12.9; APP s3; s4 Flow step 3; s8 BR2; s9; s11; s12.2
description: The branch compares the route amount with the case owner's limit in force and no source publishes the limit, its boundaries, the levels that cover an amount, the matrix row that carries them or the operation that answers them. The owner is read two ways inside this run: the sibling inside-limit story of this service (RWB-S1-E4008-APP and -CON) reads the rule, the limit and the limit version on the rwb-decision row and names rwb-decision as the owner of the authority matrix and its limit versions, while the below-floor approval story of rwb-treatment reads the Ownership Map row delegation_limit as P4 rwb-access. Architecture v5 slide 3 names the DoA Matrix v2 and no owner. The baseline and the application story read the limit on one row, declare the access row as the documented alternative, write no value, boundary or default, and carry the choice as an assumption until an owner confirms it.
evidence: FSD S1 A2.9.3.1 gives BR-S1-009 and VR-S1-009-1 only and no limit; the legacy Data table of RWB-E4-009 lists recovery_case, assignment, decision_log_entry and rule_row and no delegation row; TSD S1 T3.1 declares valuation and score only, and T6.1 gives the capability area and its rights with no limit row; RWB-S1-E4008-APP s2, s12.2 and -CON s3 read the limit on the rwb-decision row; RWB-S2-E3003-APP s2 cites the Ownership Map row delegation_limit with owner P4; Architecture v5 slide 3 states 'an approver within their delegated authority (DoA Matrix v2)'.
area: Contract, API and reference data, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: P4 rwb-access owner and P7 rwb-decision owner
proposed: The two owners confirm which service publishes the delegation row and its level, and the branch reads that one row, one hop and 2 s, with its version recorded; the other row is dropped from the baseline in a minor version and no limit value enters any document.

title: No D6 route-decision rule row is published and no S1 rule package is in force for the committee approval
source: Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (route sets and universal rules); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.9.3.1, A2.9.4.1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.2, T8); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-009)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s8 BR4; s11 Data; s14. APP s3; s4 Flow step 3; s7 Acceptance criteria; s8 BR2 and BR5; s9; s13 Configuration and reference data
description: Both legacy criteria require the result to be written with the rule version, and no rule row of the route decision is published: the routing logic carries route sets for the seven routes, the deviations and the universal rules and no route-decision set, and the D6 decision appears only as a decision code on the rows of other route sets. No S1 rule package is in force, and the TSD traceability table points every requirement of the module to FEAT-VAL-01 with the wording 'Written one epic ahead'. The story therefore records the decision code D6, the delegation version and the rule id with its version only where the decision owner provides one, and asserts no rule id of its own.
evidence: The Rules sheet of Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 holds 448 rules in ten route sets - Restructure, Settlement, Deed in lieu, Guarantee claim, Litigation, Asset disposal, Debt sale, Write-off, Deviations and Universal rules - and no route-decision set; FSD S1 A2.9.3.1 gives BR-S1-009 and VR-S1-009-1 and no rule id; TSD S1 T8 maps REQ-S1-001 to REQ-S1-008 to FEAT-VAL-01 with the story cell 'Written one epic ahead'; the sibling stories of this service record the S1 package as Phase 2.
area: Rules and reference data, S1 rwb-valuation
owner_role: P7 rwb-decision owner with the business owner of module S1
proposed: The rule owner publishes the D6 route-decision rows and the S1 package, or confirms that the decision stays a governed code with the delegation version; the record then carries that rule id and version with no change to any criterion, step or test.

title: No source names where the committee resolution, its reference and the elapsed clock are stored after the split
source: _work/msr/context/S1.md (ownership rows of S1); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T3.1, T3.3); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-009 Data); Recovery Workbench Business Rules and Routing Logic v4 (R-UNI-15)
section: CON s1; s8 BR7; s11 Data; s12.7 Tables owned; APP s2; s8 BR7; s11 Data; s12.7
description: The legacy story writes decision_log_entry, which is the ledger's and P7's, and the ownership rows give S1 no table at all, so after the split nothing holds the committee's resolution, its reference and the clock it ran under except the local decision record. TSD S1 T3.1 declares only valuation and score, and no source names an approval table for the route decision, while the restructure and debt-sale paths of the same run treat the approval record as rwb-decision's. The baseline therefore declares the resolution as an element of the decision record and writes no table and no column, and the application story records the resolution there.
evidence: The legacy Data table of RWB-E4-009 lists recovery_case, assignment, decision_log_entry and rule_row; the ownership rows of the context pack list no table under S1; TSD S1 T3.1 declares valuation and score only and T3.3 gives no approval relationship; R-UNI-15 names the one-working-day clock and no store for the answer.
owner_role: S1 rwb-valuation service owner with the P7 rwb-decision owner and the data steward
proposed: The data owner names the element or the record field that holds the resolution, its reference and the clock; if a column or a table is confirmed it arrives with the DB story of this service and the writer fills it, and until then the values live in the decision record only.

title: The legacy permission table gives right U to four officer roles and names no right for the committee that answers the route
source: 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench User Stories Epics 3 to 8 v3.md (RWB-E4-009 Permission checks, Endpoints); Recovery Workbench FSD S1 Valuation and route v3 (A2.9.3.3); Recovery Workbench TSD S1 Valuation and route v2 (T6.1)
section: CON s3 Preconditions; s8 BR9; s12.1 REST operations provided. APP s2; s3; s7 Acceptance criteria; s8 BR4; s10 Authority; s12.1
description: The legacy story carries the committee's act and grants the operation to four officer roles only: the permission table rows Treatment and offer, right U, for RW-CASEOWN, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-SPECIAL and RW-GUARANT, and the Endpoints row repeats the same right for the same path. The role that answers above the limit is the credit approval committee member, and TSD S1 T6.1 gives RW-CREDCOMM and RW-PRODHEAD right RA in the same capability area, with FSD A2.9.3.3 naming the committee member as primary and the product head as also uses. The branch therefore declares two rights, U to submit and RA to answer, and records the difference instead of widening the legacy table by invention.
evidence: Legacy RWB-E4-009 Permission checks: Treatment and offer | U | RW-CASEOWN, RW-RESTRUCT, RW-SPECIAL, RW-GUARANT; legacy Endpoints: POST /api/recovery/v1/cases/{caseId}/route | Treatment and offer U; TSD S1 T6.1: RW-PRODHEAD Product head (Mortgage, HP, SSME) RA, RW-CREDCOMM Credit approval committee member RA, RW-CASEOWN CRU, RW-RESTRUCT CRUA, RW-SPECIAL CRU, RW-GUARANT CRU; FSD S1 A2.9.3.3: Credit approval committee member Primary, Product head (Mortgage, HP, SSME) Also uses.
owner_role: P4 rwb-access owner with the business owner of module S1
proposed: The access matrix confirms right RA for the committee member and the product head on this operation and keeps right U with the four officer roles who submit; the confirmed rows replace the declared pair in a minor version with no behaviour change.
